claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'Configuration Section, IV-31' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Nucleus, VI-9'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'Configuration Section, IV-31' then '  Nucleus, VI-9'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of PDF page 964 (index page B-52) shows two columns of index entries with sub-entries indented under their main entry. The markdown transcription of page 964 holds every entry with the same text and page references, one per line, and keeps each sub-entry under its main entry with a two-space indent (e.g. 'Configuration Section, IV-31' / '  Nucleus, VI-9'; 'Control break' / '  CONTROL clause, XIII-15' ...; 'Data Division, IV-33' / '  Communication module, XIV-2' ...). The claim's quotes of both sources are accurate. The claim itself concedes that the entry text and page references match. The only difference is Markdown markup: there are no '- ' list markers, so a CommonMark renderer would fold the lines into one paragraph, and pages 961-962 use list markers that 963-966 lack. That affects how the page renders and how consistent the pages are with each other. It does not change the transcribed content: the source text keeps every entry, its line boundary and its hierarchy, and this informative index carries no normative meaning. By the verification rules, a formatting-only difference that does not change meaning is not a content discrepancy.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. On page 964 the index entries are bare lines without '- ' list markers, and sub-entries are indented with two spaces. Pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items. The text, page references and hierarchy all match the PDF. This is a rendering and consistency issue in the Markdown only.
